name: RockTrucker Hat, Black Mesh
title: Black Mesh Trucker Hat for Tree Crews
meta: A black mesh trucker hat for tree crews: a breathable mesh back, a structured front and a snapback fit for ground days, drive time and hot summer brush work.
tagline: A breathable black mesh trucker cap for ground work, travel days and the shop.
summary: The RockTrucker is a black mesh trucker hat for tree workers who want shade and airflow on ground days. The mesh back vents heat while you drag brush or run the chipper, and the snapback lets you set the fit quickly.
highlights: Black color hides sap and dirt
Curved brim for sun and glare

body.h: A cap for the ground crew
p: A mesh trucker hat earns its spot on hot days. The front panel and brim keep sun off your face while you feed the chipper, rake up or spot the climber, and the mesh back lets heat escape instead of trapping sweat under a solid crown. Black hides sap stains and bar oil better than lighter colors.
The snapback adjusts in seconds, so it fits over short or long hair and can be loosened after a long day. Browse other hats and caps if you want a stocking cap for winter or a lower-profile look.

body.h: Where it fits and where it does not
p: A ball cap is for ground work, travel and the shop. It is not head protection. When you climb, run a saw, work under a climber or stand in the drop zone, wear a helmet that meets the standard your employer and ANSI Z133 require, and keep the cap in the truck.

Hand wash with mild soap and cool water and let it air dry on its own shape. A washing machine can bend the brim and break down the front panel. Rinse sweat and sap out after summer work so the mesh stays soft and the band does not stiffen.

faq.q: Can I wear a trucker hat under my climbing helmet?
faq.a: Generally no. A cap brim can change how a helmet sits and fits. Follow your helmet maker's instructions; most allow only a thin liner or nothing at all.

faq.q: How do I clean a mesh trucker hat?
faq.a: Hand wash in cool water with mild soap, rinse well and air dry. Avoid the dryer and the washing machine, which can warp the brim.

name: Arborwear Double Thick Hooded Sweatshirt, Orange, Large
title: Arborwear Hoodie: Double Thick Sweatshirt, Orange, Large
h1: Arborwear Hoodie: Double Thick Hooded Sweatshirt, Orange, Large
meta: This Arborwear hoodie is the Double Thick hooded sweatshirt in orange, size large: two layers of heavy fabric for cold tree work, with a bright color crews can spot.
tagline: Arborwear's two-layer heavyweight hoodie in a bright orange, size large.
summary: This Arborwear hoodie is the Double Thick hooded sweatshirt in orange, size large. Two layers of fabric add warmth and toughness for winter climbing and ground work, and the orange color is easy for your crew to pick out.
highlights: Orange color is easy to spot on the ground
Roomy cut for layering and climbing
Hood for wind on cold days

body.h: Why crews wear the Double Thick
p: The Arborwear Double Thick hoodie is built with two layers of fabric, so it holds more heat than a regular sweatshirt and shrugs off bark, brush and rope longer. It works as an outer layer on cold, dry days and as a mid layer under a shell when the weather turns.

The cut leaves room to reach overhead, throw line and step up onto a limb. If you are between sizes, think about the base layer you wear under it. Other colors and styles are in our sweatshirts and jackets section.

Orange is easier for a ground crew to see than navy or black, which helps when you are moving around the drop zone or a chipper. It is still not a certified high-visibility garment. For roadside work, wear an approved vest over it as your traffic control plan requires.

Tuck drawstrings and keep the hood down under your helmet so nothing catches on rope or branches, and never reach toward a chipper infeed. Wash cold, inside out, and dry low or hang dry so the color holds.

faq.q: Does an orange hoodie count as high-visibility clothing?
faq.a: No. It is easier to see than dark colors, but it is not rated to ANSI/ISEA 107. Wear a certified vest for roadside work.

faq.q: How does the Arborwear hoodie fit?
faq.a: It has a roomy work fit meant for layering. Most people order their usual size.

name: Class 3 Safety Vest
title: Class 3 Safety Vest for Roadside Tree Work
meta: A class 3 safety vest gives roadside tree crews the most visible background and retroreflective tape. When you need Class 3, how it fits and how to keep it bright.
tagline: High-visibility vest for crews working near fast traffic or in low light.
summary: A class 3 safety vest is the high-visibility option tree crews reach for when they work beside busy roads, at night or in bad weather. It adds more fluorescent background and reflective tape than a Class 2 vest, so drivers see you sooner.
highlights: Fits over a hoodie or jacket
For roadside, flagging and low-light work
Lightweight enough to wear all day

p: ANSI/ISEA 107 sorts high-visibility garments into classes by how much fluorescent background and reflective material they carry. Class 3 is the top tier and is generally called for when traffic is fast, visibility is poor or the worker is busy with a task, like a flagger or a ground person feeding a chipper next to a lane.

Check the label before you rely on it. A true Class 3 garment states its class and type on the tag. Your traffic control plan and local rules decide what class you need, so ask your supervisor if you are not sure.

Size it to go over your heaviest winter layer so it closes fully; an open vest shows less color. Keep it away from chipper infeeds and spinning equipment, and replace it if it tears. See more cold-weather sweatshirts and jackets that layer under a vest.

Fluorescent color fades with sun and washing, and reflective tape cracks over time. Wash per the label, skip bleach, and retire the vest when it looks dull or the tape no longer shines back in headlights.

faq.q: What is the difference between a Class 2 and Class 3 vest?
faq.a: Class 3 garments carry more fluorescent background and reflective material for higher-risk settings. Your traffic control plan or employer sets the required class.

faq.q: How long does a safety vest last?
faq.a: It depends on sun and washing. Replace it when the color fades, the tape cracks or it is torn.

name: Arbortec Heavy Duty Webbing Belt
title: Arbortec Heavy Duty Webbing Belt for Work Pants
meta: The Arbortec heavy duty webbing belt holds up work and chainsaw pants without a bulky leather buckle under your saddle. Fit, use and care for tree crews explained.
tagline: A tough webbing trouser belt that sits flat under a climbing saddle.
summary: The Arbortec belt is a heavy duty webbing trouser belt for tree workers. It holds work pants or chainsaw trousers in place with a low profile that sits more comfortably under a saddle than a thick leather belt.
highlights: Low profile under a saddle waist belt
Holds up work and chainsaw trousers
Easy to wash and dries fast

body.h: A belt that works with a saddle
p: A thick leather belt and a big buckle can press into your hips under a saddle waist belt. A webbing belt lies flatter, bends with you and does not soak up sweat the same way. The Arbortec belt is made to hold up heavy work pants and chainsaw trousers through a full day of climbing, dragging and bucking.
It pairs well with any of the tree climbing pants we carry. Many climbers run a belt and suspenders together on heavy chainsaw trousers.

body.h: Not part of your climbing system
p: This is a trouser belt only. It is not a positioning belt or fall protection, and you should never clip a lanyard, rope or tool to it as a life-support point. Clip life-support gear only to the rated attachment points on your saddle, follow the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and get proper training.
Rinse out sweat and sap now and then and let it air dry. Replace it if the webbing frays or the buckle stops holding.

faq.q: Can I wear this belt under my saddle?
faq.a: Yes. That is what a low-profile webbing belt is for. Check that the buckle does not sit under a saddle buckle or bridge attachment.

faq.q: Is a webbing belt rated for fall protection?
faq.a: No. It only holds up your pants. Use your rated saddle for anything life-support.

name: Arborwear Ascender Pants, Driftwood
title: Arborwear Ascender Pants, Driftwood: Climbing Pants
meta: Arborwear Ascender pants in driftwood are stretch climbing pants for big steps, long hours in a saddle and rough bark. How they fit, wear and compare to other pants.
tagline: Stretch climbing pants in a light driftwood tone for long days aloft.
summary: Arborwear Ascender pants are stretch work pants made for tree climbers, here in a light driftwood color. They move with you on high steps and limb walks and sit comfortably under saddle leg loops.
highlights: Stretch fabric for high steps and wide stances
Cut to work under a climbing saddle
Tough enough for bark and rope wear
Driftwood color stays cooler in sun

body.h: Made to move in a tree
p: Stiff canvas fights you when you step up onto a limb or spread your feet across a crotch. The Ascender uses stretch fabric and a climbing cut so you can move freely without the pants binding at the knee or pulling at the waist. It sits comfortably under leg loops and a saddle waist belt for hours.

Driftwood is a light tan that reflects more sun than coal or black, which helps on summer jobs. It shows sap a little more, so expect a working patina. The same pant comes in darker colors, and our tree climbing pants page covers heavier and lighter options.

Try them with your saddle on if you can. A good climbing fit is snug at the waist and roomy through the thigh, with pockets that do not sit under a leg loop. Empty heavy items from pockets before you go up.

These are work pants, not chainsaw protection. When you run a saw on the ground, wear chaps or chainsaw-protective pants as ANSI Z133 requires. Wash cold, hang dry or tumble low, and check crotch and knee seams regularly so small tears get fixed early.

faq.q: Are Arborwear Ascender pants cut resistant?
faq.a: No. They are climbing work pants. Wear chaps or chainsaw pants when running a saw on the ground.

faq.q: How do Ascender pants fit under a saddle?
faq.a: They are cut for climbing, so the waist and thighs sit comfortably under saddle belts and leg loops. Most people order their normal waist size.

name: Arborwear Canopy Pants, Coal
title: Arborwear Canopy Pants, Coal: Tree Work Pants
meta: Arborwear Canopy pants in coal are work pants for climbers and ground crews that hold up to bark, brush and rope. See fit, care and how they compare to other pants.
tagline: Arborwear's tree work pant in a dark coal color that hides the dirt.
summary: Arborwear Canopy pants are work pants made for tree care, here in a dark coal gray. They are cut to move when you climb and tough enough for dragging brush and kneeling on rough ground.
highlights: Cut for climbing and ground work
Durable fabric for bark and brush
Coal color hides sap and bar oil

body.h: A daily pant for tree work
p: The Canopy is one of Arborwear's tree work pants, designed for people who climb in the morning and drag brush all afternoon. The cut leaves room through the seat and thigh for big steps, and the fabric is made to take bark, rope and chipper-side work without wearing through in a season.

Coal is a dark charcoal that hides sap, bar oil and stump dirt, so the pants look presentable at the next job. If you want a lighter color for summer sun, the Canopy also comes in driftwood. Compare it with other tree climbing pants for stretch and weight.

Try them on with your saddle or compare against a pair you already like. You want the waist snug and the pockets clear of leg loops. Wash cold and inside out to slow fading, and hang dry or tumble low.

These are work pants, not chainsaw protection. When you run a saw on the ground, wear chaps or chainsaw-protective pants as ANSI Z133 requires. Check seams at the crotch and knees now and then and repair small tears before they spread.

faq.q: Are Arborwear Canopy pants chainsaw pants?
faq.a: No. They are work pants with no cut protection. Wear chaps or chainsaw pants when running a saw on the ground.

faq.q: Can I climb in Canopy pants?
faq.a: Yes. They are cut for tree work and sit comfortably under a saddle.

name: Arborwear Canopy Pants, Driftwood
title: Arborwear Canopy Pants, Driftwood: Tree Work Pants
meta: Arborwear Canopy pants in driftwood: tree work pants in a light tan that stays cooler in the sun, cut for climbing and tough on brush. Fit, care and typical price.
tagline: Arborwear's tree work pant in a light driftwood tan for sunny jobs.
summary: Arborwear Canopy pants in driftwood are tree work pants in a light tan that stays cooler under summer sun. They are cut for climbing and built to handle brush, bark and rope.
highlights: Light color for hot, sunny days
Cut for climbing and ground work
Durable fabric for bark and brush

body.h: A lighter color for summer work
p: Dark pants soak up heat on an open removal in July. Driftwood is a light tan that reflects more sun, which many climbers prefer for summer. The tradeoff is that sap and bar oil show more, so treat these as working pants and expect a little character.

The Canopy cut gives room through the seat and thigh for climbing and kneeling, and the fabric holds up to the bark and brush that shred cheap work pants. The same pant comes in coal, and our tree climbing pants page lists other weights and styles.
Order your usual waist size and check that pockets clear your saddle leg loops. Pre-treat sap with a degreaser or hand cleaner before washing, wash cold, and hang dry or tumble low.

These are work pants, not chainsaw protection. When you run a saw on the ground, wear chaps or chainsaw-protective pants as ANSI Z133 requires. Inspect crotch and knee seams regularly and fix small tears early.

faq.q: Does driftwood show dirt?
faq.a: More than coal does. Pre-treat sap and oil before washing to keep them looking clean.

faq.q: Are Canopy pants cut resistant?
faq.a: No. Wear chaps or chainsaw pants when running a saw on the ground.

name: Arborwear Original Tree Climbers' Pants, Chestnut
title: Arborwear Original Tree Climbers' Pants, Chestnut
h1: Arborwear Original Tree Climbers' Pants, Chestnut
meta: Arborwear Original Tree Climbers' Pants in chestnut: heavy cotton canvas work pants with a gusseted crotch, built for climbers who are hard on gear. Fit, care, price.
tagline: Arborwear's heavy canvas climbing pant in a warm chestnut brown.
summary: The Arborwear Original Tree Climbers' Pants are heavy cotton canvas pants built for climbers who wear out ordinary work pants, here in chestnut brown. A gusseted crotch gives room to step up, and the heavy fabric takes bark and rope abuse.
highlights: Built for hard climbing and brush work
Breaks in and softens with wear

p: The Original Tree Climbers' Pants are the heavy canvas option in the Arborwear lineup. The fabric is stiff out of the bag and breaks in over a few weeks of climbing and washing. In exchange you get a pant that stands up to spurs on bark, rope over the knee and long days dragging brush.

A gusseted crotch adds room so you can step high without the seam pulling. Chestnut is a warm brown that hides dirt and sap. If you prefer stretch, compare the lighter options on our tree climbing pants page.
Heavy cotton can shrink a little in hot water, so wash cold and dry low or hang dry. Order your usual size and expect a stiff feel at first. Make sure pockets do not sit under saddle leg loops.

These are work pants, not chainsaw protection. When you run a saw on the ground, wear chaps or chainsaw-protective pants as ANSI Z133 requires. Check the seams and knees as they age and patch wear early.

faq.q: Are the Original Tree Climbers' Pants stiff?
faq.a: Yes, at first. Heavy canvas softens with washing and wear over a few weeks.

faq.q: Do they protect against chainsaw cuts?
faq.a: No. Wear chaps or chainsaw pants when running a saw on the ground.

name: Clogger Spider Pants, Contrast Color
title: Clogger Spider Pants, Contrast Color: Arborist Work Pants
meta: Clogger Spider pants in contrast color are arborist work pants from the Australian maker Clogger, built for climbing and brush work. Fit, care and what to check.
tagline: Clogger's Spider arborist pant in contrast color, made for tree crews who move a lot.
summary: Clogger Spider pants are arborist work pants from Clogger, the Australian maker best known for chainsaw protective clothing, shown here in contrast color. They are cut for climbing and ground work and built to handle bark, brush and rope.
highlights: Arborist cut for climbing and ground work
Made by Clogger, a specialist in tree-work clothing
Built for bark, brush and rope wear
Check the label for any cut-protection rating

p: Clogger designs clothing specifically for arborists, and the Spider pant follows that approach: room through the seat and knee for high steps, fabric meant to stand up to bark and rope, and a fit that works with a saddle. The contrast-color version adds a brighter panel color so ground crew can pick you out against bark and foliage.

If you are choosing between several pairs, compare fabric weight, stretch and pocket layout across our tree climbing pants. Climbers who spend all day aloft usually favor stretch and lighter weight; ground crews often want tougher fabric.

Clogger makes both chainsaw-protective trousers and general work clothing. Read the label on your pair: chainsaw pants state the standard they meet and the protected area. If no cut-protection standard is listed, treat them as work pants and wear chaps or chainsaw pants when you run a saw on the ground, as ANSI Z133 requires.
Wash per the care label, keep fuel and solvents off the fabric, and inspect seams and high-wear areas regularly.

faq.q: Are Clogger Spider pants chainsaw pants?
faq.a: Check the label. Clogger chainsaw trousers state the protection standard they meet. Without that, wear chaps or chainsaw pants when running a saw.

faq.q: How do Clogger pants size?
faq.a: Clogger uses its own size chart, and sizing can differ from US work pants. Measure your waist and inseam and compare before ordering.

name: Edelrid Easy Glider Belt, Night
title: Edelrid Easy Glider Belt, Night: Low-Profile Pants Belt
meta: The Edelrid Easy Glider belt in night is a low-profile webbing trouser belt for climbers that adjusts quickly and sits flat under a saddle. Fit, use and care.
tagline: A slim, quick-adjust webbing trouser belt from Edelrid in a dark night color.
summary: The Edelrid Easy Glider belt is a slim webbing trouser belt for climbers and outdoor workers, here in a dark night color. It adjusts quickly and lies flat, so it stays comfortable under a saddle waist belt.

body.h: A belt you forget you are wearing
p: Edelrid comes from the climbing world, and the Easy Glider is the kind of belt climbers like: slim webbing that lies flat, a buckle that adjusts without fixed holes, and no bulk to press into your hips under a saddle. It holds up work pants on the ground and stays out of the way when you are aloft.
The night color is a dark shade that matches most work and climbing pants. Pair it with any of our tree climbing pants.

This belt holds up pants. It is not a harness component and is not rated for fall protection or work positioning. Clip ropes, lanyards and life-support hardware only to the rated points on your saddle, follow the manufacturer's instructions and ANSI Z133, and train before you climb.
Rinse out sweat and grit now and then and let it air dry. Replace it if the webbing frays or the buckle starts to slip.

faq.q: Will the Easy Glider belt sit under my saddle?
faq.a: Yes, its slim profile is designed to be comfortable under a saddle waist belt. Keep the buckle clear of saddle buckles and attachment points.

faq.q: Is the Edelrid Easy Glider belt a climbing harness?
faq.a: No. It is a trouser belt with no fall-protection rating.

name: Teufelberger wayUP Light Climbing Pants
title: Teufelberger wayUP Light Climbing Pants
meta: Teufelberger wayUP Light climbing pants are lightweight tree climbing pants made to move with you on hot days and long climbs. Fit, use, care and what to look for.
tagline: Lightweight climbing pants from Teufelberger for warm days and long climbs.
summary: The wayUP Light is one of the Teufelberger climbing pants, a lighter-weight pant for climbers who want freedom of movement and less heat on summer jobs. It is designed to sit comfortably under a saddle through long days aloft.
highlights: Cut for high steps and limb walking
From a major arborist rope and gear maker

p: Teufelberger is best known for climbing rope and saddles, and its climbing pants come from the same focus on how arborists move. The wayUP Light is the lighter option, aimed at summer climbing and long days aloft where a heavy canvas pant feels like a sauna.

A lighter pant gives up some abrasion resistance compared with heavy canvas, so it suits climbers who spend more time in the tree than dragging brush. Compare weights and fabrics on our tree climbing pants page.

Try the pants with your saddle on and take a high step. They should not pull at the knee or seat, and pockets should clear your leg loops. European sizing can run differently from US waist sizes, so check the size chart.

These are work pants, not chainsaw protection. When you run a saw on the ground, wear chaps or chainsaw-protective pants as ANSI Z133 requires. Wash per the label and inspect the seams and knees as the pants age.

faq.q: Are the wayUP Light pants chainsaw protective?
faq.a: No. Wear chaps or chainsaw pants when running a saw on the ground.

faq.q: Are lightweight climbing pants durable enough for ground work?
faq.a: They hold up to normal climbing, but heavy canvas lasts longer if you spend most days dragging brush.

name: Pfanner Protos Bluetooth Communication System
title: Pfanner Protos Bluetooth Headset Communication System
meta: The Pfanner Protos Bluetooth headset adds hands-free talk between climber and ground crew to a Protos Integral helmet. How it fits, works and what to check before buying.
tagline: Bluetooth headset add-on for Protos Integral helmets, for climber-to-ground talk.
summary: This Protos Bluetooth headset is Pfanner's communication system for the Protos Integral helmet. It fits into the helmet's ear protection so climbers and ground crew can talk hands-free over saw and chipper noise.
highlights: Made for the Pfanner Protos Integral helmet
Hands-free talk between climber and ground
Works with the helmet's hearing protection

p: Hand signals and yelling work until a saw is running and the chipper is chewing. A helmet headset lets the climber call the next piece, tell the groundie to hold or let run, and hear the answer clearly. The Protos system is built into the ear protection of the Protos Integral helmet, so there is no loose earpiece or cord to snag.
It is designed for Protos helmets; confirm your helmet model before you order. Other headsets and radios are on our communication page.

body.h: Use it as a tool, not a crutch
p: Agree on clear calls and a backup plan before the work starts, and stop work if the link drops during rigging. Communication between climber and ground is a core part of ANSI Z133 practice; a headset makes it easier but does not replace a job briefing or a trained crew.
Keep the volume low enough that the hearing protection still does its job. Charge the unit overnight and follow Pfanner's instructions for fitting and care.

faq.q: Does the Protos Bluetooth system fit other helmets?
faq.a: It is made for Pfanner Protos Integral helmets. Check compatibility with your exact helmet before buying.

faq.q: Can the whole crew talk at once?
faq.a: That depends on the setup and how many units you pair. Check Pfanner's instructions for the intercom options supported.

name: Fanno 17" Tri-Edge Pole Saw Blade
title: Fanno 17" Tri-Edge Pole Saw Blade
meta: The Fanno 17 inch tri-edge pole saw blade is a fast-cutting replacement blade for pole saw heads. Fit, cutting feel and how to swap and care for it on the job.
tagline: A 17-inch tri-edge replacement blade for pruning pole saws.
summary: This Fanno pole saw blade is a 17-inch tri-edge replacement blade for pole saw heads. Tri-edge teeth cut on the pull stroke and clear chips well, so it moves quickly through green limbs overhead.
highlights: Tri-edge teeth for fast pull cuts
Made by Fanno, a US saw maker

body.h: A fresh edge for your pole saw
p: A dull pole saw blade turns a clean pruning cut into a fight, and on a pole every extra stroke is wasted effort at arm's length. The Fanno 17-inch tri-edge blade gives you a new set of teeth for your pole saw head. Tri-edge teeth are ground on three faces, cut on the pull and clear sawdust well in green wood.
Before ordering, check that the mounting holes and blade length match your saw head. More replacement blades are listed in our blades section.

Replace the blade when teeth are dull, bent or broken, or when the blade has a kink. Swap it on the ground with the pole laid down. Wear gloves when you handle a bare blade, keep it in a scabbard or cover when it is not in use, and never cut toward your body or your lanyard.

Wipe off sap after use and keep the blade dry to prevent rust. Never use a pole saw near energized power lines unless you are a trained, qualified line-clearance arborist with the right equipment, and keep the minimum approach distances in ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Will this blade fit my pole saw?
faq.a: It fits pole saw heads made for a 17-inch blade with matching mounting holes. Check your head before ordering.

faq.q: Can I sharpen a tri-edge blade?
faq.a: Tri-edge teeth are usually hardened and hard to file well. Most crews replace the blade when it dulls.

name: Jameson 16" Tri-Cut Saw Blade
title: Jameson 16" Tri-Cut Pole Saw Blade
meta: The Jameson 16 inch tri-cut saw blade is a replacement pole saw blade for Jameson saw heads, built for fast pull cuts in green wood. Fit, use and care explained.
tagline: A 16-inch tri-cut replacement blade for Jameson pole saw heads.
summary: This Jameson pole saw blade is a 16-inch tri-cut replacement for Jameson saw heads. The tri-cut teeth cut on the pull stroke and move quickly through green limbs when you are pruning from the ground.
highlights: Tri-cut teeth for fast pull cuts
Replacement for Jameson pole saw heads

p: Jameson pole saws are common on tree crews and utility trucks, and the blade is the part that wears out. A fresh 16-inch tri-cut blade brings back fast, clean cuts. The teeth cut on the pull, which is the natural stroke when you are working overhead from the ground.
Check that the blade length and mounting pattern match your saw head before you order. More options are in our blades section.

Change the blade on the ground with the pole laid flat. Replace it when teeth are dull, missing or bent, or if the blade is kinked from a pinch. Wear gloves when you handle a bare blade, keep it in a scabbard or cover when it is not in use, and never cut toward your body or your lanyard.

Clean off sap and keep the blade dry. Never use a pole saw near energized power lines unless you are a trained, qualified line-clearance arborist with the right equipment, and keep the minimum approach distances in ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Does this blade fit non-Jameson saw heads?
faq.a: It is made for Jameson heads. Other heads may use different lengths or hole patterns, so compare before buying.

faq.q: When should I replace a pole saw blade?
faq.a: When it cuts slowly, drifts in the cut, or has bent, broken or missing teeth.

name: Replacement Blade for HS-13TE-LPS Hand Saw
title: Replacement Blade for HS-13TE-LPS Hand Saw
h1: Replacement Blade for HS-13TE-LPS Hand Saw
meta: An HS-13TE replacement blade for the HS-13TE-LPS 13 inch hand saw. Swap a dull or kinked blade and keep the handle and scabbard you already own. Fit and care notes.
tagline: A replacement 13-inch blade for the HS-13TE-LPS pruning hand saw.
summary: This HS-13TE replacement blade fits the HS-13TE-LPS 13-inch pruning hand saw. When the teeth go dull or the blade gets kinked, a new blade puts the saw back in service without buying a whole new saw.
highlights: Made for the HS-13TE-LPS hand saw
Keeps your existing handle and scabbard in use
Cheaper than replacing the whole saw

body.h: A new blade for a saw you already know
p: Hand saw blades wear out long before the handle does. Pruning in dirty bark, cutting near the ground and hitting the odd nail all dull teeth, and a pinch can put a kink in the blade that makes it bind. This replacement blade is made for the HS-13TE-LPS hand saw, so you keep the grip and scabbard you are used to and get fresh teeth.
Check the model number on your saw before ordering; blades from different saws rarely interchange. Other replacement blades are in our blades section.

Swap the blade on the ground or at the truck, not aloft. Tighten the fasteners firmly and check the blade does not wobble before you cut. Wear gloves when you handle a bare blade, keep it in a scabbard or cover when it is not in use, and never cut toward your body or your lanyard.
Wipe sap off after use, keep the blade dry and store the saw in its scabbard. A clean blade cuts faster and lasts longer.

faq.q: Will this blade fit other 13-inch saws?
faq.a: It is made for the HS-13TE-LPS. Other saws often use different mounting holes, so match the model before buying.

faq.q: Can I resharpen the old blade?
faq.a: Hardened pruning-saw teeth are hard to file well. Most climbers replace the blade.

name: Silky Gomtaro Pro Sentei Replacement Blade
title: Silky Gomtaro Pro Sentei Replacement Blade
h1: Silky Gomtaro Pro Sentei Replacement Blade
meta: A Silky Gomtaro replacement blade for the Gomtaro Pro Sentei pruning saw. Bring back a sharp straight blade without buying a new saw. Fit, swap and care notes.
tagline: Fresh straight blade for the Silky Gomtaro Pro Sentei pruning saw.
summary: This Silky Gomtaro replacement blade fits the Gomtaro Pro Sentei straight pruning saw. Silky saws keep their handles for years, so a new blade is the simple way to get back the clean, fast cut you bought it for.
highlights: Made for the Silky Gomtaro Pro Sentei
Keeps your handle and scabbard in service

p: The Gomtaro is one of Silky's straight-blade workhorses, and the Pro Sentei version is popular with climbers and pruners who want a stiff blade that tracks straight. Silky teeth are hard and very sharp, but they do dull, especially in dirty bark or dead wood. A replacement blade gets the saw cutting like new for less than a whole saw.
Match the blade length to your saw before you order. Other Silky and pole saw blades are listed in our blades section.

Swap blades at the truck with the saw on a flat surface, and tighten the fasteners firmly. Wear gloves when you handle a bare blade, keep it in a scabbard or cover when it is not in use, and never cut toward your body or your lanyard.
Silky blades cut on the pull, so let the saw do the work and do not force the push stroke. Wipe off sap after use and keep the blade dry to stop rust.

faq.q: Does this blade fit other Gomtaro models?
faq.a: Gomtaro saws come in several lengths and tooth patterns. Match the blade to your exact saw before buying.

faq.q: Can Silky blades be sharpened?
faq.a: Silky teeth are impulse hardened and are not meant to be filed. Replace the blade when it dulls.

name: Silky Hayate 390mm XL Teeth Replacement Blade
title: Silky Hayate 390mm XL Teeth Replacement Blade
h1: Silky Hayate 390mm XL Teeth Replacement Blade (Blade Only)
meta: A Silky Hayate replacement blade: 390 mm with extra-large teeth for the Hayate telescoping pole saw. Fast cuts in big green limbs. Fit, swap and care notes inside.
tagline: A 390 mm extra-large-tooth blade for the Silky Hayate telescoping pole saw.
summary: This Silky Hayate replacement blade is the 390 mm version with extra-large teeth, sold as a blade only. It fits the Hayate telescoping pole saw and is built to move quickly through larger green limbs from the ground.
highlights: Fits the Silky Hayate pole saw
Extra-large teeth for fast cuts in green wood

p: The Hayate is Silky's telescoping pole saw, and the 390 mm extra-large-tooth blade is the aggressive choice for it. Big teeth take a large bite with each pull, which is what you want for clearing green limbs overhead. The tradeoff is a rougher cut face than a finer tooth, so some climbers keep a second blade for finish pruning.
This is the blade only. Confirm you have the Hayate before ordering. Other pole saw and hand saw blades are in our blades section.

Change the blade on the ground with the pole collapsed and laid flat. Check that it is seated and the fasteners are tight before you extend the pole. Wear gloves when you handle a bare blade, keep it in a scabbard or cover when it is not in use, and never cut toward your body or your lanyard.

Wipe off sap and keep the blade dry. Never use a pole saw near energized power lines unless you are a trained, qualified line-clearance arborist with the right equipment, and keep the minimum approach distances in ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Will this blade fit other Silky pole saws?
faq.a: It is made for the Hayate. Other Silky pole saws use different mounts, so check your model first.

faq.q: Should I choose extra-large or regular teeth?
faq.a: Extra-large teeth cut faster in green wood. Finer teeth leave a cleaner face on pruning cuts and handle dry wood better.

name: Silky Hayate Sickle Replacement Blade
title: Silky Hayate Sickle Replacement Blade (Blade Only)
h1: Silky Hayate Sickle Replacement Blade (Blade Only)
meta: The Silky Hayate sickle blade is a replacement hook blade for the Hayate pole saw, used to cut vines, suckers and small shoots overhead. Fit, use and care notes.
tagline: Replacement sickle blade for the Silky Hayate pole system, for vines and small shoots.
summary: The Silky Hayate sickle blade is a replacement hook-style blade for the Hayate pole system, sold as a blade only. A sickle edge is useful for slicing vines, water sprouts and small shoots that a saw blade snags on.
highlights: Replacement sickle blade for the Silky Hayate
Hook shape for vines and small shoots
Pairs with your existing Hayate pole

body.h: For the stuff a saw hates
p: Saw teeth are made for wood. Vines, suckers and soft shoots tend to flex away from a saw and wrap around the blade. A sickle edge hooks the material and slices it on the pull, which is faster and cleaner for that kind of clean-up work.
Confirm the blade matches your Hayate before ordering, as Silky's pole saws use different mounts. Saw blades for the Hayate and other saws are in our blades section.

Change blades on the ground with the pole collapsed. Make sure the blade is seated and secure before you extend the pole. A sickle edge is sharp along its whole length, so wear gloves and keep the cover on when it is not in use.

Wipe it clean and dry after use. Never use a pole saw near energized power lines unless you are a trained, qualified line-clearance arborist with the right equipment, and keep the minimum approach distances in ANSI Z133.

faq.q: What is a sickle blade used for?
faq.a: Cutting vines, sprouts, suckers and small soft growth that saw teeth tend to snag on.

faq.q: Does it come with a pole?
faq.a: No. It is a blade only for use with the Silky Hayate.

name: Silky Pocketboy Replacement Blade
title: Silky Pocketboy Replacement Blade
meta: A Silky Pocketboy replacement blade puts a sharp edge back in your folding saw. Match length and tooth size to your Pocketboy, then swap in minutes. Fit and care notes.
tagline: Fresh blade for the Silky Pocketboy folding pruning saw.
summary: A Silky Pocketboy replacement blade brings your folding saw back to full sharpness without buying a new saw. Pocketboy saws come in different lengths and tooth sizes, so match the blade to your model.
highlights: Fits the Silky Pocketboy folding saw
Match length and tooth size to your saw
Keeps a favorite saw in service

p: The Pocketboy is a compact folding saw that lives in a lot of pockets and gear bags, used for small pruning cuts, clearing a throw line path and quick clean-up. Because it gets used for everything, the teeth wear. A replacement blade costs much less than a new saw and brings the cut back.
Pocketboy saws are made in more than one length and with different tooth sizes. Check your current blade, then order the match. Other blades are in our blades section.

Swap the blade on a flat surface, tighten the pivot and check that the lock engages fully before you cut. Wear gloves when you handle a bare blade, keep it in a scabbard or cover when it is not in use, and never cut toward your body or your lanyard.
Fold the saw closed whenever you put it down. Wipe sap off the blade and keep it dry so the pivot does not gum up.

faq.q: Which Pocketboy blade do I need?
faq.a: Match the length and tooth size printed on your current blade or saw.

faq.q: Can I sharpen a Pocketboy blade?
faq.a: Silky teeth are hardened and not meant to be filed. Replace the blade instead.

name: Fanno Wooden Handle 13" Hand Saw
title: Fanno Wooden Handle 13" Pruning Hand Saw
meta: The Fanno hand saw with a wooden handle and 13 inch blade is a classic pruning saw for climbers and ground crews. How it cuts, who it suits, care and safety notes.
tagline: A US-made 13-inch pruning saw with a traditional wooden handle.
summary: This Fanno hand saw pairs a 13-inch pruning blade with a traditional wooden handle. Fanno makes its saws in the US, and this one is a straightforward tool for pruning cuts aloft and limbing on the ground.
highlights: Made by Fanno in the USA

p: Plenty of climbers still like the feel of a wooden handle: it stays warm in winter, does not get slick the way some plastics do, and fits the hand naturally. The Fanno 13-inch saw pairs that handle with a blade long enough for most pruning cuts and short enough to manage one-handed for positioning.
Thirteen inches is a common size for climbers because it reaches through cuts in 4 to 6 inch limbs without being awkward on a saddle. Compare it with other options in our hand saws and scabbards.
When you carry a hand saw aloft, keep it in a scabbard on your saddle and make two-handed cuts away from your rope and lanyard. Follow ANSI Z133 and get trained before you climb.
Wipe sap off after the job and keep the blade dry. A wooden handle lasts longer if you do not leave it soaking in a wet truck bed. Check that the blade fasteners stay tight.

faq.q: Is a wooden handle better than a rubber one?
faq.a: It comes down to feel. Wood stays warm and firm; rubber grips well when wet and absorbs some vibration.

faq.q: Does this saw come with a scabbard?
faq.a: Check the listing. If not, pick a scabbard that fits a 13-inch blade and clips securely to your saddle.

name: Jameson 11" Straight Blade Hand Saw
title: Jameson 11" Straight Blade Pruning Hand Saw
meta: The Jameson hand saw with an 11 inch straight blade is a compact pruning saw for small cuts aloft and on the ground. Who it suits, how it cuts and how to care for it.
tagline: A compact 11-inch straight pruning saw for small cuts and tight spaces.
summary: This Jameson hand saw has an 11-inch straight blade, a compact size for small pruning cuts, crown cleaning and work in tight spots. It is light on the saddle and easy to control with one hand.
highlights: Compact and light on the saddle
Straight blade tracks well in tight spots

body.h: A compact saw for detail work
p: Not every cut needs a 13-inch blade. Crown cleaning, small deadwood and fine pruning cuts often happen in tight spots where a shorter saw is easier to control. The Jameson 11-inch saw is sized for that work and weighs less on your saddle.

A straight blade tracks predictably and works well for cuts at or below shoulder height. For bigger limbs or cuts overhead, a longer curved saw is often faster. Browse our hand saws and scabbards to compare.
When you carry a hand saw aloft, keep it in a scabbard on your saddle and make two-handed cuts away from your rope and lanyard. Follow ANSI Z133 and get trained before you climb.
Clean off sap after use and keep the blade dry. Replace the blade or saw when teeth are dull or the blade has a kink.

faq.q: Is an 11-inch saw big enough for climbing?
faq.a: It handles small pruning and crown cleaning well. Many climbers carry it alongside a longer saw for bigger cuts.

faq.q: Straight or curved blade?
faq.a: Straight blades track predictably and suit cuts at or below shoulder level. Curved blades bite more aggressively, especially overhead.

name: Jameson 13" Ergonomic Handle Hand Saw
title: Jameson 13 Inch Hand Saw with Ergonomic Handle
meta: The Jameson 13 inch hand saw with an ergonomic handle is a full-size pruning saw that is comfortable through a long day of cuts. Who it suits, care and safety notes.
tagline: A full-size 13-inch pruning saw with a shaped grip for long days.
summary: This Jameson 13 inch hand saw has a shaped ergonomic handle that is easier on your hand through a long day of pruning. The 13-inch blade reaches through most limbs a climber cuts by hand.
highlights: Full-size saw for most hand cuts

body.h: Comfort for a day of cuts
p: A pruning job can mean hundreds of saw strokes. A shaped grip spreads the load across your hand and helps you keep control when your forearm starts to tire. The Jameson ergonomic handle is built for that, and the 13-inch blade handles most limbs you would cut by hand rather than with a top-handle saw.
If you prefer the feel of wood, Jameson also makes this saw with a wooden handle. Compare both in our hand saws and scabbards.
When you carry a hand saw aloft, keep it in a scabbard on your saddle and make two-handed cuts away from your rope and lanyard. Follow ANSI Z133 and get trained before you climb.
Wipe off sap and keep the blade dry. Retire or re-blade the saw when it starts to drift in the cut or the teeth are damaged.

faq.q: What size limbs can a 13-inch hand saw cut?
faq.a: It handles most limbs a climber would cut by hand. For larger wood, use an appropriate saw and technique.

faq.q: Will it fit my existing scabbard?
faq.a: Most scabbards made for 13-inch saws will fit, but check the blade shape and length before you rely on it.

name: Jameson 13" Wooden Handle Hand Saw
title: Jameson 13" Wooden Handle Pruning Hand Saw
meta: The Jameson wooden handle hand saw has a 13 inch pruning blade and a classic wood grip that stays warm and firm. Who it suits, how it cuts, care and safety notes.
tagline: A 13-inch pruning saw with a classic wooden grip.
summary: The Jameson wooden handle hand saw pairs a 13-inch pruning blade with a classic wood grip. It is a simple, dependable saw for pruning aloft and limbing on the ground.
highlights: Full-size saw for most hand cuts

p: Wood handles have a following among climbers for good reasons: they stay warm in cold weather, they do not feel tacky in heat, and they wear in to your hand. This Jameson saw pairs that grip with a 13-inch blade, the size many climbers settle on for everyday pruning.
If you want a shaped grip instead, Jameson makes an ergonomic-handle version. Compare both, plus Silky and Fanno saws, in our hand saws and scabbards.
When you carry a hand saw aloft, keep it in a scabbard on your saddle and make two-handed cuts away from your rope and lanyard. Follow ANSI Z133 and get trained before you climb.
Keep the handle out of standing water, wipe sap off the blade and store it dry. Replace the saw or blade when it dulls or kinks.

faq.q: Will the wooden handle get slippery?
faq.a: Wood grips well in most conditions. Wear gloves and keep sap off the handle for a secure hold.

faq.q: Is 13 inches a good size for a climbing saw?
faq.a: Yes. It is one of the most common climbing sizes, long enough for most hand cuts and still easy to carry.

name: Silky Pocketboy 130 Folding Saw, Large Teeth
title: Silky Pocketboy 130 Folding Saw, Large Teeth
h1: Silky Pocketboy 130 Folding Saw, Large Teeth
meta: The Silky Pocketboy 130 is a compact folding saw with a 130 mm blade and large teeth for fast cuts in small green limbs. Who it suits, how to carry it and care.
tagline: A pocket-size Silky folding saw with a 130 mm blade and large teeth.
summary: The Silky Pocketboy 130 is a compact folding saw with a 130 mm blade, here with large teeth for fast cuts in green wood. It folds small enough for a pocket or gear bag and is handy for small cuts and clean-up.
highlights: Large teeth for fast cuts in green wood
Folds small for a pocket or bag

p: The Pocketboy 130 is the saw you carry when you do not want to carry a saw. It handles small pruning cuts, clearing twigs from a throw line path, trimming a stub, and odd jobs around the truck. The large-tooth blade bites fast in green wood; finer teeth leave a smoother cut in dry wood.
For regular climbing work, most arborists still carry a full-size saw in a scabbard. See our hand saws and scabbards for 13-inch options.

Make sure the blade locks fully open before every cut, and fold it closed before you pocket it. Do not use it as a primary climbing saw on a lanyard cut; keep cuts small and controlled, away from your rope and lanyard.
Wipe off sap and keep the pivot clean. When the teeth dull, fit a Pocketboy replacement blade that matches the length and tooth size.

faq.q: Large or medium teeth?
faq.a: Large teeth cut faster in green wood. Finer teeth cut smoother and handle dry wood better.

faq.q: Can I replace the blade?
faq.a: Yes. Silky sells replacement Pocketboy blades; match the length and tooth size.

name: Silky Gomtaro 300mm Hand Saw
title: Silky Gomtaro 300mm Straight Hand Saw with Scabbard
meta: The Silky Gomtaro 300mm is a straight-blade pruning hand saw with a scabbard, known for fast, clean cuts and a stiff blade. Who it suits, care and safety notes.
tagline: Silky's popular straight 300 mm pruning saw, sold with a scabbard.
summary: The Silky Gomtaro 300mm is a straight-blade pruning saw that comes with a scabbard. It is a long-time favorite with climbers and landscapers for fast, clean pull cuts and a stiff blade that tracks straight.

body.h: Why the Gomtaro is so common
p: The Gomtaro is one of the saws that made Silky popular with tree crews. The straight 300 mm blade is stiff, so it tracks well and is less prone to wandering in the cut. The Japanese pull-stroke teeth cut quickly and leave a clean face, which matters on pruning cuts.

A straight blade is easy to control below shoulder height and in tight spots. If you do more overhead cutting, a curved Silky like the Zubat may suit you better. Compare in our hand saws and scabbards.
When you carry a hand saw aloft, keep it in a scabbard on your saddle and make two-handed cuts away from your rope and lanyard. Follow ANSI Z133 and get trained before you climb.
Let the pull stroke do the work and avoid forcing the push. Wipe sap off after use. When the teeth dull, fit a replacement Gomtaro blade instead of buying a new saw.

faq.q: Can the Gomtaro blade be sharpened?
faq.a: Silky teeth are impulse hardened and are not designed to be filed. Replace the blade when it dulls.

faq.q: Does it come with a scabbard?
faq.a: Yes, the Gomtaro is normally sold with a scabbard.

name: Silky Tsurugi Curved Hand Saw, Medium Teeth
title: Silky Tsurugi Curved Hand Saw, Medium Teeth
h1: Silky Tsurugi Curved Hand Saw, Medium Teeth
meta: The Silky Tsurugi is a curved pruning hand saw, here with medium teeth for a balance of speed and finish on pruning cuts. Who it suits, how it cuts and care notes.
tagline: A curved Silky pruning saw with medium teeth for clean, quick cuts.
summary: The Silky Tsurugi is a curved pruning saw, shown here with medium teeth. The curve helps the blade bite on overhead cuts, and medium teeth balance cutting speed with a clean face on pruning cuts.
highlights: Medium teeth for speed and finish

p: A curved blade pulls itself into the wood, which helps on overhead cuts and on limbs you reach from an awkward stance. Medium teeth are a good all-round choice: fast enough for green limbs, smooth enough to leave a clean pruning cut that seals well.

Silky offers several curved saws at different lengths and tooth sizes. Choose the length that suits your typical cuts and how you carry it on your saddle. Compare options in our hand saws and scabbards.
When you carry a hand saw aloft, keep it in a scabbard on your saddle and make two-handed cuts away from your rope and lanyard. Follow ANSI Z133 and get trained before you climb.
Wipe sap off after the job, keep the blade dry, and swap in a replacement blade when the teeth dull.

faq.q: Curved or straight Silky saw?
faq.a: Curved saws bite aggressively and suit overhead work. Straight saws track predictably and suit lower cuts and tight spots.

faq.q: Does the Tsurugi come with a scabbard?
faq.a: It is normally sold with one. Check the listing before buying.

name: Silky Zubat Arborist Edition 13" Hand Saw
title: Silky Zubat Arborist Edition 13" Hand Saw
h1: Silky Zubat Arborist Edition 13" Hand Saw
meta: The Silky Zubat Arborist Edition is a 13 inch (330 mm) curved climbing saw paired with an arborist scabbard. How it cuts, how it rides on a saddle, and care notes.
tagline: Silky's 13-inch curved Zubat set up for climbers with an arborist scabbard.
summary: The Silky Zubat Arborist Edition is the 13-inch (330 mm) curved Zubat saw set up for tree climbers with an arborist-style scabbard. It is one of the most common climbing hand saws on tree crews.

p: The Zubat is a curved 330 mm saw with aggressive pull-stroke teeth that cut green wood very quickly. The curve lets the blade bite on overhead cuts and helps it stay engaged when you are cutting from an awkward position. The Arborist Edition pairs it with a scabbard designed to ride on a saddle.
If you mostly cut at or below shoulder height in tight spots, a straight blade like the Gomtaro may suit you better. Compare in our hand saws and scabbards.

When you carry a hand saw aloft, keep it in a scabbard on your saddle and make two-handed cuts away from your rope and lanyard. Follow ANSI Z133 and get trained before you climb. The Zubat cuts fast, so keep your free hand and your lanyard well clear.
Wipe sap off after use, keep the blade dry, and swap in a replacement Zubat blade when the teeth dull.

faq.q: What is different about the Arborist Edition?
faq.a: It pairs the 13-inch Zubat with a scabbard designed for arborists to carry on a climbing saddle.

faq.q: Can I buy a replacement Zubat blade?
faq.a: Yes. Silky sells replacement Zubat blades in matching lengths and tooth patterns.

name: 12" Pruner Rope Insulator
title: 12" Pruner Rope Insulator for Pole Pruners
meta: A 12 inch pruner rope insulator is a non-metallic link for the pull rope on a pole pruner. What it does, where it fits, and its limits near power lines explained.
tagline: A 12-inch non-metallic link for the pull rope on a pole pruner.
summary: A pruner rope insulator is a short non-metallic link that goes in the pull rope of a pole pruner, here in a 12-inch length. It breaks up a wet or dirty rope run and is part of a properly set up pole pruner.
highlights: Non-metallic link for the pruner pull rope
Part of a standard pole pruner setup

p: Pole pruners use a pull rope to close the cutting head. A rope that is wet, dirty or worn can carry current, so many pruner setups include a non-metallic insulator link in the rope run. If yours is cracked, missing or worn, this is the replacement part.
Fit it according to your pruner's instructions and check the rope at both ends for wear. Poles, ferrules and other parts are on our poles and kits page.

An insulator link does not make a pole tool safe to use near power lines. Work near energized conductors is for trained, qualified line-clearance arborists using equipment rated and tested for that purpose, keeping the minimum approach distances in ANSI Z133 and following OSHA rules. Everyone else stays out of the zone and calls the utility.
Keep the insulator clean and dry and replace it if it is cracked, chipped or contaminated.

faq.q: Does a rope insulator make my pole pruner safe near power lines?
faq.a: No. Only qualified line-clearance arborists with properly rated and tested tools may work near energized lines, and they must keep ANSI Z133 approach distances.

faq.q: When should I replace the insulator?
faq.a: When it is cracked, chipped, contaminated or badly worn, or if the rope attachment points are damaged.

name: Sentei 16' 3-Section Telescoping Aluminum Pole Saw
title: 16' Sentei 3-Section Telescoping Aluminum Pole Saw
meta: A 16 foot telescoping pole saw with a three-section aluminum pole for pruning from the ground. Reach, handling, care and why aluminum stays well away from power lines.
tagline: A 16-foot, three-section aluminum telescoping pole saw for ground pruning.
summary: This Sentei telescoping pole saw extends to about 16 feet on a three-section aluminum pole. It lets a ground worker or climber reach small limbs and deadwood without moving a ladder or setting a line.

p: A telescoping pole saw is the fastest way to deal with low limbs, small deadwood and clearance pruning over a driveway or sidewalk. Three sections collapse for the truck and lock out to the length you need, up to about 16 feet. Work below the limb and to the side, so cut pieces drop clear of you.
A long pole is harder to control at full extension, so extend only as far as the job needs. Sectional fiberglass poles and parts are on our poles and kits page.

Aluminum conducts electricity. Never use this pole saw anywhere near overhead lines, service drops or anything that could be energized. Line-clearance work requires qualified arborists with insulated, tested tools and ANSI Z133 approach distances.
Wear a helmet and eye protection, since debris falls toward you. Keep the locks clean, wipe sap off the blade, and replace the blade when it dulls.

faq.q: Can I use an aluminum pole saw near power lines?
faq.a: No. Aluminum conducts electricity. Stay well away from any line and call a qualified line-clearance arborist.

faq.q: How high can a 16-foot pole saw reach?
faq.a: Add your own reach to the pole length, but control drops off at full extension. Cut only what you can control.

name: Female Ferrule with Spring Clip
title: Female Ferrule with Spring Clip for Sectional Poles
meta: A female ferrule with spring clip joins sectional pruning poles with a snap-lock fit. What it does, how to check yours and when to replace it, plus safety notes.
tagline: Replacement female pole ferrule with a spring-clip lock for sectional poles.
summary: A female ferrule with spring clip is the socket end of a sectional pruning pole joint. The spring button on the mating male ferrule snaps into it, locking the sections together so the pole does not twist or pull apart.
highlights: Female (socket) half of a pole joint
Replaces a worn or damaged ferrule

p: Sectional poles connect through metal ferrules: a male end with a spring button and a female socket that the button snaps into. A worn or bent ferrule lets sections wobble, twist or separate, which makes the pole hard to control and can drop the saw head. This is the female half for replacing a damaged socket.
Match the ferrule to your pole's diameter and connection style before ordering. Poles and kits are on our poles and kits page.

Install it per the pole maker's instructions so it is fully seated and secure. Before each use, check that every joint locks with a click and does not rotate. Clean grit out of the socket so the spring clip engages fully.
Metal ferrules conduct electricity. Do not use sectional poles near power lines unless you are a qualified line-clearance arborist using tested equipment and keeping ANSI Z133 approach distances.

faq.q: How do I know if my ferrule needs replacing?
faq.a: If the joint wobbles, twists, will not click, or the socket is bent or cracked, replace it.

faq.q: Will this fit any pole?
faq.a: Ferrules are made for specific pole diameters and connection styles. Match yours before ordering.
